newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan leads Canada in provincial GDP growth.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan leads Canada in provincial GDP growth.

text.p: Saskatchewan led Canada's 10 provinces in the growth of gross domestic product in 1996, with a 3.3 percent increase, Statistics Canada said on Friday.
The province's performance was based on agriculture and sustained strength in oil and gas production, the federal agency said.
Two other western provinces were close behind, with GDP growing by 2.9 percent in Manitoba and 2.6 percent in Altberta, oupacing the national average gorwth rate of 1.5 percent for 1996.

Newfoundland was the only province in which production fell, declining 0.9 percent, as ecnomic benefits from the construction phase of the Hibernia oil project waned and government cutbacks remained in force, StatsCan said.
